subsystems.name: Ground laser array
subsystems.role: generates and steers the pushing beam.

subsystems.name: Light sail
subsystems.role: reflects laser light and converts photon momentum into thrust.
parts: metamaterial coating tuned to the laser wavelength

subsystems.name: Star-chip probe
subsystems.role: carries sensors and communication on a gram-scale payload.

subsystems.name: Deployment stage
subsystems.role: carries the sail and probe to space and releases them.

subsystems.name: Communication and tracking
subsystems.role: sends the laser beam and later receives the probe's faint signals.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sail
buildSteps.detail: Deposit a thin film of silicon nitride or similar on a substrate, pattern it with a reflective metamaterial, and etch away the substrate to leave a free-standing membrane just hundreds of nanometres thick.

buildSteps.title: Build the laser array
buildSteps.detail: Assemble thousands of fibre lasers or solid-state amplifiers, phase-lock them so their light combines into a single coherent beam, and direct it through a large segmented mirror.

buildSteps.title: Make the star-chip
buildSteps.detail: Integrate a camera, a tiny computer, a laser transmitter and a power source onto a single chip a few centimetres across, weighing a few grams.

buildSteps.title: Attach sail to probe
buildSteps.detail: Mount the chip at the centre of the sail, fold or stow the sail for launch.

buildSteps.title: Launch to orbit
buildSteps.detail: Use a conventional rocket to place the carrier into low Earth orbit or higher.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in space
buildSteps.detail: Release the sail and probe, spin-stabilize it if needed, and point it toward the laser array.

buildSteps.title: Accelerate
buildSteps.detail: Fire the laser array at the sail, ramping power over several minutes to push the probe to about 20% of light speed.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and return data
buildSteps.detail: The probe coasts to Alpha Centauri for about 20 years, takes images during a flyby, and sends them back by laser, arriving about 4 years later.

prerequisites.why: solar sails have flown (e.g., LightSail 2) but not laser-driven at this power and scale.

prerequisites.tech: Phase-locked laser arrays at gigawatt power
prerequisites.why: no such array exists; current laser arrays are far lower power and not coherent over kilometres.

prerequisites.tech: Precise beam pointing and adaptive optics
prerequisites.why: astronomical telescopes use adaptive optics, but pointing a laser at a sail moving at 20% c requires extreme precision.
chip-scale satellites exist, but not with light-year-range laser communication.

prerequisites.tech: Power source for the laser array
prerequisites.why: grid-scale power plants can supply gigawatts, but the cost and infrastructure would be enormous.

pathway.milestone: solar sail flights (LightSail 2) and conceptual studies like Breakthrough Starshot
pathway.unlocks: basic demonstration of photon pressure in space.

pathway.milestone: ground laser arrays of increasing power pushing small sails in orbit for station-keeping or debris removal
a demonstration accelerating a gram-scale probe to a few percent of light speed within the solar system
pathway.unlocks: fast interplanetary missions and validation of the full system.

pathway.milestone: a full-scale laser array and sail launching a probe to Alpha Centauri at 20% light speed
pathway.unlocks: first interstellar flyby and data from another star system.
